newsitem.title: USA: Read-Rite shrs firm, but off earlier high.
newsitem.headline: Read-Rite shrs firm, but off earlier high.

text.p: Shares in takeover target Read-Rite Corp settled into a narrow range between 33-1/2 and 33-5/8 from 32 in midsession Nasdaq trade, retreating from an earlier peak of 36-1/4, the highest point since November 1995.

At midday, the almost 6.3 million shares traded was more than twice Read-Rite's average daily volume, activity driven by Applied Magnetics Corp's hostile, stock-swap takeover bid announced last night, traders said.
Read-Rite said its board will meet today to consider the proposal, which values Read-Rite at about $33.85, based on Applied's current stock price of 49-7/8.
Including today's three-point decline on the NYSE, Applied shares have fallen from 58 since last Thursday, although the stock is up from 30 from the beginning of 1997.
Applied is offering to exchange 0.679 of a share for each Read-Rite share to create a leading maker of computer disk drive heads with an estimated $1.8 billion in annual revenues.
Based on Friday's closing prices, the offer represented a 33 percent premium for Read-Rite shareholders, a payoff that has narrowed with the stocks' recent price moves.
When Applied announced its bid after the market close yesterday, it said it had been attempting to craft a friendly transaction with Read-Rite for nine months, but had been rebuffed.

Gruntal & Co analyst David Takata said in a research note, "We see this proposed merger validating our view that the industry would continue to consolidate as the capital investments required to be a major player continue to rise."

Applied "suggests a merger of the two head makers would yield a company with about 30 percent of the total industry head business ... which should clear (federal) antitrust tests," according to the analyst.
He pointed out that the merged company would "still be heavily dependent on Western Digital Corp as a greater-than-50 percent-of-sales customer still focused on making thin-film desktop drives."
Shares in Western Digital, supplier of disk drives to computer makers, fell 3-3/8 at 68-5/8 in afternoon NYSE trade.

"Bottom line, the proposed merger is good for Read-Rite shareholders. Although there is still an opportunity for Read-Rite's management to negotiate with Applied or to seek a different merger that might be equally beneficial or better for shareholders, we see nothing wrong with cashing in on the deal as presented," Takata noted.
